install.help:
Steve native management CLI

  steve setup [hub|node] [--home PATH] [--listen 0.0.0.0:8440] [--public-url URL]
              [--adapters ID,ID|all|none]
              [--hub https://hub.example] [--pin sha256:FINGERPRINT]
              [--label LABEL] [--vault-dir PATH] [--fresh]
  steve setup [hub] --reconfigure [--home PATH] [--listen IP:port]
  steve hub|node start|stop|restart|status|doctor|uninstall [--home PATH] [--label LABEL] [--json]
  steve hub|node install --release PATH [--home PATH] [--label LABEL]
  steve node update --release PATH [--wait SECONDS]
  steve upgrade check|request|status|watch [--home PATH] [options]
  steve adapters status|upgrade [hub|node] [--home PATH]
  steve adapters install ID [ID...] [hub|node] [--home PATH]

Every command takes --lang zh-CN|en; without it the language follows STEVE_LANG, LANG, then the system language.

On a terminal, setup is a wizard: choose the role, the network and the ACP adapters to install; it can start the Hub when it is done.
setup listens on 0.0.0.0:8440 by default and derives the Web address from the listen address (--public-url sets it, --reconfigure changes it later).
When the data directory already holds an installation of another version, the wizard asks whether to install fresh; --fresh does so directly: the old service is stopped and unregistered,
and the whole directory is renamed to <directory>.bak-<time> and kept; no data is deleted.
Off a terminal (a pipe, TERM=dumb, STEVE_PLAIN=1) setup only registers the service and does not start it; it never imports login credentials or grants a Node working directories.
--reconfigure only maintains the network and the existing OIDC configuration of an installed Hub, keeping secrets, identity and data; it does not restart anything.
Service commands print a summary on a terminal; a pipe or --json keeps the JSON output.

Do not delete the receipt or reset the data directory to get around this check.
